q: What is the energy use per tonne for MSME glass and refractory units by cluster?
title: Glass and refractory units: energy per tonne
short: It depends mostly on what you make. BEE's energy mapping found 10.4 GJ per tonne across Firozabad glass, 25.3 GJ for Ambala's blown glass and 1.6 GJ for Jaipur's toughening, with Chirkunda refractories at 5.7 GJ and East and West Godavari at 6.7 GJ.
audience: Glass, bangle, scientific glassware and refractory makers comparing their energy per tonne with their cluster

ul: Firozabad glass: 1,061,920 t a year, 249 kgoe (10.4 GJ) per tonne.
East and West Godavari refractories: 62,530 t, 159 kgoe (6.7 GJ).
Glass blowing, Ambala: 27.5 GJ per tonne.
Decorative and other glass, Firozabad: 8.0 GJ.
Toughened glass, Jaipur: 1.7 GJ, since it reheats bought sheet rather than melting batch.
Refractories: Chirkunda downdraft kilns 6.23 GJ and tunnel kilns 4.19 GJ; Godavari downdraft kilns 6.66 GJ.

p: Glass used 276,777 toe and refractories 105,446 toe. The study lists automatic combustion control, better furnace and kiln insulation, waste heat recovery and switching from solid fuel to gas, then pot arching for glass, downdraft to tunnel kilns for refractories, electric furnaces, kilns and lehrs, and rooftop solar. It also proposes common facilities for bangle baking and refractory sintering.

ul: Fuel in GJ from your bills plus power at 3.6 MJ per kWh, divided by tonnes packed or fired in the same year.
These figures cover energy only. Soda ash, limestone and dolomite in a glass batch give off CO2 as they melt; add that from batch weights.

example.title: A Firozabad container glass unit, 20,000 t a year
lines: Gas: 4,000,000 scm x 0.0398 GJ (9,500 kcal per scm on the bill) = 159,200 GJ
Energy per tonne: 180,800 / 20,000 = 9.0 GJ, about 17% above the 7.7 GJ container average
Energy CO2: 4,000,000 x 2.05 = 8,200 t; 6,000,000 x 0.675 = 4,050 t; 0.61 t per tonne before batch CO2
example.note: An example unit, not a measured one: use your own bills. Gas and grid factors are our estimates, the grid at CEA's FY 2025-26 figure.

senseible: Senseible reads your gas and electricity bills into yearly energy and CO2 records, each linked to its bill, which you divide by tonnes to compare with these cluster figures.
